clue.text: A person may be entitled to start with this

definitions.text: A person may be entitled to start with this

parts.words: A person may be entitled to start with this
parts.note: something one is entitled to from the very start of life, by virtue of being born

explanation.surface: A remark about what someone can claim at the outset of some venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' suggests the beginning of a task, but here it is the start of life itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An inheritance or privilege owed to someone from the moment they are born is exactly what the phrase describes.

clue.text: Knowing about home side at The Oval

parts.note: at home means in
the on side is one half of a cricket field, such as The Oval's

explanation.surface: Someone well informed about the home team at a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground; in cricket the field is split into the off side and the on (leg) side.
explanation.definitionFit: To be party to a secret or plan is an idiom meaning aware of it or privy to it.

clue.text: That's bad university teacher putting off men repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly means the remaining piece occurs twice in a row
putting off means sending away, so these letters are removed

parts.note: a tutor teaches at a university
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Disapproval of a lecturer who keeps postponing meetings with staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting off' removes OR (other ranks, i.e. men) from TUTOR, leaving TUT, which 'repeatedly' doubles.
explanation.definitionFit: The interjection is an exclamation of disapproval, a way of saying something is wrong.

clue.text: Devil-may-care group of fliers — brill?

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force
brill is a flatfish, an example of a fish

explanation.surface: Asking whether a daring squadron of pilots is brilliant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brill' looks like slang for brilliant, but it is the flatfish; the question mark flags the example.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a carefree, rakish, slightly disreputable attitude to life.

clue.text: Win one more time with leader absent

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which is missing here

parts.note: one more time means again

explanation.surface: A wish to triumph again, only without the team captain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with leader absent' removes the first letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain or earn something, such as a prize, is a synonym for the verb in the clue.

clue.text: Plant person on field to get stuck into work

indicators.note: getting stuck into something means going inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: toil is hard work
a referee, ref for short, officiates on the playing field

explanation.surface: A sports official who is told to plant themselves on the pitch and get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb telling the official where to stand, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Clover and similar three-leaved herbs belong to this plant group.

clue.text: Downplay what citizens of repressive regime are?

definitions.meaning: to downplay is to present something as less important than it is

definitions.text: what citizens of repressive regime are?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, people under a harsh government live beneath the power of the nation

explanation.definitionFit: Representing something as smaller than it is means downplaying, while the split reading describes people ruled by a powerful government.

clue.text: Argue against prisoner time and time again wanting to keep dog?

parts.note: a con is a convict

indicators.note: wanting to keep means holding something inside, so the two time letters enclose the dog

parts.note: a second T for time
Rover is a traditional name for a dog

explanation.surface: A convict who repeatedly wishes to keep a pet in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting to keep' puts ROVER between the two Ts; Rover is the stock dog's name, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute or contradict a claim is a formal synonym for arguing against it.

clue.text: Wreck international organisation over allowing 500 in

indicators.note: allowing a thing in means letting it inside, so one piece is placed within the others
in completes the phrase allowing ... in, marking the insertion

parts.note: the UN is the United Nations
O is the cricket abbreviation for over
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A global body accused of ruining things by letting in hundreds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman numeral D goes between UN and O.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin or bring to nothing someone's work is a sense of the verb, as in being one's own downfall.

clue.text: Job cancelled with frigidity in public building

parts.note: a post is a job
an event that is off has been cancelled
ice embodies coldness

explanation.surface: Someone laid off coldly from a job in a government building.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where mail is handled and stamps are sold is a familiar public building.

clue.text: Most splendid poem about dwelling in a tree?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the poem's title reads backwards

parts.note: If is Rudyard Kipling's famous poem
a bird's nest is a home in a tree

explanation.surface: Praising a poem written about a treehouse as the best.
explanation.walkthrough: The poem is Kipling's 'If'; 'about' turns it to FI.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of a word meaning excellent, so of the highest quality.

clue.text: Very large lady by front of hotel who welcomes guests?

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
Tess is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A large woman standing at the entrance of a hotel to greet visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the pieces together: H is put first, giving H + OS + TESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who receives and entertains visitors is the female equivalent of a host.

clue.text: Language in Indian huts possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a language is spoken in dwellings in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue of northern India, related to both Hindi and Urdu, is the language named.

clue.text: What offers an 'edgy' performance accompanied by music?

definitions.text: What offers an 'edgy' performance accompanied by music?

parts.words: What offers an 'edgy' performance accompanied by music?
parts.note: a dance performed to music over or with sharp blades has an edge in a literal sense

explanation.surface: A question about a nervy show set to music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edgy' seems to mean tense, but refers to blades with sharp edges.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland dance stepped around crossed blades is literally a performance featuring edges.

clue.text: Boy in holy band getting healthy food?

parts.note: SA is the Salvation Army, a religious body famed for its brass bands
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy in a church band choosing something wholesome to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of raw vegetables and leaves is commonly seen as a nutritious option, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Small illustration, a ship, by old artist

parts.note: pic is short for picture
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: A little picture of a ship by an old master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just puts the pieces next to each other.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism is a famous example of an artist.

clue.text: Safe foundation for church

definitions.meaning: in criminal slang a strongbox or safe has this name
the apostle Jesus named the rock on which he would build his church

explanation.surface: A church whose foundations are secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Safecrackers' slang names a strongbox thus, and the apostle is the Gospel's rock upon which the church is built.

clue.text: Girl in state of confusion left

parts.note: a haze is a muddled state of mind

explanation.surface: A girl who walked out in a daze.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female given name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Limited number operating — twelve

parts.note: No. is the shortened form of the word number
a machine that is on is operating

explanation.surface: Only a few machines running, a dozen at most.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock, so the time is a fair stand-in for the number.

clue.text: Report of rude person in the nude

indicators.note: report means something said out loud, so the word is to be heard

parts.note: a bear is a gruff, ill-mannered person

explanation.surface: News of a boorish man spotted naked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unclothed is a synonym for being naked.

clue.text: Pale little man declined

parts.note: wan means pale
Ed is short for Edward, a man's name

explanation.surface: A pallid small man turned down an offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Diminished or faded, as the moon does, is a synonym of declined.

clue.text: What settles the clothes being put on outside

indicators.note: something put on outside goes round the rest, so it encloses the other letters

parts.note: wear means clothing, as in menswear

explanation.surface: Getting dressed by putting clothes on to go out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settles' is cryptic: we speak of the conditions outdoors settling when it turns calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmospheric conditions are said to settle into a calm spell, so this is what settles.

clue.text: Dad swimming with ease? He wouldn't be, in this lake!

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters moving about in the water

explanation.surface: Father bobbing easily in salty water, where he could not sink.
explanation.walkthrough: Its water is so salty that a bather floats rather than swimming, hence 'He wouldn't be'.
explanation.definitionFit: The salt lake between Israel and Jordan is the body of water meant.

clue.text: Not taken out, not having the time?

definitions.meaning: someone never asked on a romantic outing
a letter or document without a date written on it

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking a date describes both someone not escorted on an outing and a document with no time recorded.

clue.text: Money paid over period for chemical

indicators.note: over means covering, so the money goes round the period

parts.note: rent is money paid regularly
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Money handed over across a stretch of time for a laboratory substance.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance used to cause or detect a reaction in the laboratory is a type of chemical.

clue.text: Georgia slouches awkwardly in dances

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
to lop is to hang down loosely or move in a slouching way

explanation.surface: A woman named Georgia slumping clumsily on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively nineteenth-century ballroom dances in two-four time are the plural noun meant.

clue.text: Estate could provide facility for refreshment

indicators.note: could provide suggests the letters might be made into something else

explanation.surface: A country estate that might offer a café for visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Cups, saucers and a pot together equip someone to serve a refreshing drink.

clue.text: Club with hot tub

parts.note: a bat is a club used in sports
H is short for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A sports club with a hot tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel for washing in is a tub.

clue.text: Scottish location in which to plant a vegetable

indicators.note: planting something in a place means putting it inside, so one piece goes within

parts.note: a ben is a Scottish mountain

explanation.surface: Choosing a spot in Scotland to grow vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad, runner and kidney are kinds of this pulse, a common vegetable.

clue.text: Principal's ways of speaking to convey grave things

parts.note: a head is the principal of a school
tones are manners of speaking

explanation.surface: A headteacher's manner of speech conveying solemn matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like serious, but means burial place.
explanation.definitionFit: Memorial slabs set at burial plots are literally things belonging to a grave.

clue.text: Enjoyable nook with husband out of the way

indicators.note: out of the way means removed, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: a niche is a recess or nook

explanation.surface: A pleasant secluded corner once the husband has gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant or agreeable is a synonym for enjoyable.

clue.text: Somehow he's angrier getting ready for a show?

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are rearranged in some way

explanation.surface: An actor who grows more irritable before opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: Practising a play or performance beforehand is preparation for a show.
